title: The heavenly delight is an indeliberate act sent from heaven
source_text: LVIII. Quibus animadversis, observat idem Doctor coelestem delectationem, in qua ponit Christi auxilium efficax, ad omnem piam operationem & bonum voluntatis actum, necessarium, non esse delectationem illam proprie dictam, per quam voluntas in bono praesenti acquiescit, & eo fruitur; & quae est desiderii, quo voluntas fertur in bonum, quasi terminus: nec etiam ullum esse voluntatis motum liberum atque deliberatum; Sed actum quendam indeliberatum coelitus immissum in voluntatem, & per quem, vel ei bonum propositum suaviter tantum placet, vel etiam in bonum appetendum commovetur. Qui actus coelitus immissus, licet voluntas eum libere non eliciat, ab ea tamen active procedit, & vitalis est illius quidam motus.
pass_a_gloss: LVIII. Which things being noticed, the same Doctor observes that the heavenly delight, in which he places the efficacious help of Christ, necessary to every pious operation and good act of the will, is not that delight properly so called, through which the will rests in a present good, and enjoys it; and which is of desire, by which the will is borne to good, as a term: nor yet is it any free and deliberate motion of the will; But a certain indeliberate act sent from heaven into the will, and through which, either the good proposed only sweetly pleases it, or it is even moved to desiring the good. Which act sent from heaven, although the will does not elicit it freely, yet proceeds actively from it, and is a certain vital motion of it.
pass_b_english: Thesis LVIII. With these points in view, the same doctor observes that the heavenly delight in which he places Christ's efficacious aid, needed for every devout action and good act of the will, is not delight in the proper sense, by which the will rests in a present good and enjoys it and which is the end point of the desire by which the will is carried toward the good. Nor is it any free and deliberate movement of the will.

It is an indeliberate act sent into the will from heaven, through which the good put before the will either simply pleases it sweetly or even stirs it to desire that good. Although the will does not elicit this heaven-sent act freely, the act still proceeds from the will actively and is a vital movement of the will.

lemmas.latin: in qua ponit Christi auxilium efficax
lemmas.gloss: in which he places the efficacious help of Christ
a certain indeliberate act sent from heaven

choices.why: An act arising before the mind deliberates (LVII), as opposed to a free, deliberate act.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4.
